prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The monocular depth map captures a kitchen layout with a central island and stools on the left (roughly 1.5 to 3 metres away), a refrigerator on the right (within 0.3 to 1.2 metres), a sink counter along the far left wall (2 to 4 metres away), and a person in a white shirt standing in front of the camera wearer at roughly 0.8 to 1.5 metres distance. In frames 1 and 2, the standing person faces the camera wearer before turning rightward toward the refrigerator in frames 2 through 5 (with her head cropped above the top edge of the frame throughout, preventing direct sight of her gaze), while the camera wearer approaches the refrigerator and raises their left arm into the foreground (0.2 to 0.4 metres away) in frames 4 and 5, partially occluding the other person. In frame 2, the other person's left hand reaches out to touch the closed refrigerator door, and by frames 4 and 5 the open refrigerator door and interior shelves are within arm's reach of both the camera wearer and the other person. Compared to the RGB strip, the depth map much more clearly separates the foreground silhouette of the camera wearer's raised hand/arm and the open refrigerator door from the mid-ground person and background kitchen cabinetry. However, the map looks unreliable in frame 3 where the close refrigerator door saturates to uniform white and makes the person's torso appear abnormally dark and distant due to relative depth rescaling, and inside the open refrigerator in frames 4 and 5 where shelf depths and specular surfaces are blurred together.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates the foreground person in the centre-left of all five frames (roughly 0.8 to 1.5 metres from the camera wearer) and segments a bar stool ('chair') just behind her at about 1.8 metres in frame 1 and the open refrigerator interior and door on the right at 0.3 to 1.0 metre in frame 5. As the sequence progresses from frame 1 to frame 5, the segmented person turns from facing the camera wearer to facing right toward the refrigerator while her head remains cropped out above the frame and her lower legs are cropped at the bottom. While the map clearly delineates the combined outer contour of the person and the open refrigerator in frame 5, it adds little beyond the RGB image and is highly unreliable across the strip. Specifically, it completely misses the refrigerator in frames 1 to 4, mislabels a section of the kitchen island counter behind the person's right elbow as a 'sink' in frame 2, splits the person's extended left hand into a separate mask from her body in frame 2, and merges the camera wearer's own foreground left hand and raised arm (0.2 to 0.4 metres away) into the other person's mask in frames 4 and 5.
descriptions.pose: The body and hand skeleton map tracks the 2D joint positions of the person standing roughly 0.8 to 1.5 metres in front of the camera wearer against a black background that removes all kitchen furniture and appliances. In frame 1, the yellow torso and leg skeleton shows her hips and shoulders squared toward the camera wearer with her right hand (magenta) hanging down at her side, whereas in frame 3 the narrowed shoulder-hip geometry and raised right arm crossing her torso toward the right (with detailed magenta finger keypoints roughly 0.7 metres away) show she has rotated rightward toward the refrigerator door within her arm's reach. Although her head is mostly cropped above the top border in the RGB frames, frame 3 reveals estimated facial keypoints near the top edge oriented to the right away from the camera wearer, which is hard to confirm from the cropped RGB image alone. The pose map is unreliable in frames 2, 4, and 5, where motion blur and severe occlusion from the refrigerator door and the camera wearer's raised foreground arm cause the full-body skeleton to drop out completely: frame 2 contains only a stray false-positive yellow cluster in the background and a partial magenta right hand, frame 4 detects only a single raised magenta hand near the top of the refrigerator, and frame 5 is entirely blank.
